rankings.blurb: Four Cornerstones. FOUR. Jahmyr Gibbs, Drake Maye, Puka Nacua, and Trey McBride all in one place like some kind of dynasty fantasy supervillain lair. Yes, they mortgaged a small nation of picks to get Gibbs, and yes the pick cupboard is nearly bare, but when your worst starter is Kyren Williams you don't really need draft picks, do you? The only thing keeping this team from a perfect score is that overpay for Gibbs — trading two future first-rounders plus a second and Skattebo is the kind of move that either looks genius or haunts you at the championship table. Right now it looks like genius.

Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational pieces. ELEVEN. Ja'Marr Chase, JSN, Drake London, De'Von Achane, Omarion Hampton, Jayden Daniels, Justin Herbert, Trevor Lawrence — this roster reads like someone accidentally enabled god mode. The problem is Sven has been hemorrhaging draft capital lately, going 0-3 in recent trades and giving nchernandez19 the keys to a small draft kingdom, which is embarrassing. No picks is a real concern when your depth falls off a cliff after those top guys, but the elite core alone makes this a legitimate championship contender right now.

Seven first-round picks and a total dynasty value that's actually tops in this league — jsinykin is playing a completely different game than everyone else and it's honestly kind of annoying. Caleb Williams and Jaxson Dart at QB is the most exciting young quarterback room in this league, and stacking Jeremiyah Love with Quinshon Judkins at RB before anyone knew what they had is the kind of foresight that wins championships in two years. The current player value is a little thin in the win-now department with no elite proven studs outside Williams, but with Harold Fannin, Egbuka, Luther Burden, and a mountain of picks, the trajectory here is absolutely terrifying. The Reload label is technically correct but undersells how quickly this thing could explode.

Josh Allen is the single most valuable fantasy asset in the sport and gavinw20 just has him sitting there alongside Ashton Jeanty like it's nothing. The WR room of Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Jaylen Waddle is three guys who are all annoyingly good but none of them are making anyone's top-five receiver list, which is the quiet Achilles heel here. Giving up Tyler Shough and a first for Baker Mayfield and Garrett Wilson is a trade that aged about as well as a warm mayonnaise sandwich — Shough is up 20% in value since that deal. Gavin is still absolutely fine and the floor here is high, but this roster needs a WR1 to stop pretending it's a contender.

Zero first-round picks. Zero. You traded away two 2029 firsts and a second to nchernandez19 for Michael Wilson and Malik Willis and some mystery box, which is a transaction so catastrophically bad it should be framed and hung in a museum of poor decision-making. Joe Burrow and Amon-Ra are a phenomenal core and Jalen Hurts adds legitimate QB depth, but the supporting cast is a parade of aging Mainstays — Kenneth Walker, Breece Hall, Jonathan Taylor — who are all one hamstring away from being a different conversation. The Contender label is generous given you just stripped your own future and got torched by two separate trade partners in the same week.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers in the same dynasty rebuild is the most luxurious poverty anyone has ever experienced. nchernandez19 has been absolutely murdering it in the trade market lately — fleecing GiantHawkTua for two 2029 firsts and a second while giving up literal nothing of consequence is the kind of highway robbery that should come with a mask and a getaway car. Six first-round picks plus that Bijan and Bowers core means this rebuild has a legitimate runway to contend, but the QB room of Jordan Love and C.J. Stroud with question marks is the one area that could derail everything. A WR room headlined by Marvin Harrison's still-unproven NFL potential is another bet, but at least it's an exciting bet.

Seth had the audacity to sell Jahmyr Gibbs — a literal Cornerstone — for a pile of future picks, and honestly? Respect the chaos. Five first-round picks, Cam Skattebo, TreVeyon Henderson, Jadarian Price, Travis Hunter, and George Pickens is a rebuild that has actual upside attached to it. The problem is Tyler Shough at QB1 for what could be a two-year window is the dynasty equivalent of installing a screen door on a submarine — technically it's something, but you're still going underwater. George Kittle as a short-term TE1 buys some time, but this team wins in 2028 or it wins never.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb are two of the most beautiful receiver assets in dynasty and Grey has somehow built a roster around them that feels like it's held together with duct tape and desperation. Brock Purdy as your QB1 in a win-now window is a choice — a legal choice, but a choice — and the RB room of Chase Brown and a rapidly deteriorating Christian McCaffrey is a ticking clock that is definitely not ticking in your favor. No future first-round picks, a TE room that doesn't exist, and a recent trade history of giving up thirds and a Kupp to get Jerry Jeudy is the kind of portfolio management that makes financial advisors cry. The WR duo alone keeps this team out of the basement, but just barely.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes at QB is the most expensive and chaotic solution to a non-problem this league has ever seen, and yet somehow you still don't have a single first-round pick in your future because you traded your 2028 first to get Ladd McConkey from Akracoon, who immediately turned around and sold McConkey for more picks — you got played like a fiddle. A.J. Brown and Tee Higgins are fine but both are aging out of their dynasty windows, Derrick Henry is running on fumes and vibes, and Travis Kelce is showing up to his own retirement party. Zero future draft capital means when this window slams shut, it's going to shatter.

Akracoon sold Ja'Marr Chase — a 9,978 KTC Cornerstone — and turned it into Ladd McConkey, two firsts, and a second, and then immediately flipped McConkey for yet another first, which is either the best or worst thing anyone has ever done depending on your timeline. Seven first-round picks sounds great until you realize your current roster is Fernando Mendoza, Bhayshul Tuten, Quentin Johnston, and Dak Prescott's knees, which is a starting lineup so bad it would lose to a bye week. Malik Nabers is a legitimate Cornerstone and the only reason this blurb doesn't devolve into a eulogy, but with positional grades at the absolute bottom of this league across every single position, Akracoon is in line at the soup kitchen with a lot of lottery tickets. This is a 2028 problem at the earliest.
